newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger on data in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger on data in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in quiet trade on Friday, with spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowing amid the release of Canadian gross domestic product and current account data, analysts said.

"There really wasn't a lot in terms of volume going through in Canada on the session," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with Technical Data. "I wouldn't say that they (investors) could fall in love with the data but it was acceptable in terms of bidding up Canadian securities."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.25 to C$111.35 to yield 7.044 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.81 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 23 basis points from 26 basis points at Thursday's close.

"We've had some activity throughout the day, moderate activity, fairly quiet in the afternoon," said a dealer with one bank-owned brokerage. "People wanted to tidy up and buy a few bonds before the end of the month and go home early."

The slew of Canadian economic data released earlier today included a report that the country's real gross domestic product rose 0.7 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996. Economists had forecast a rise of 1.0 percent.

But the GDP data was accompanied by a report that Canada's current account deficit for the fourth quarter was lower-than-expected. Another report showed the fourth quarter GDP price deflator rose just 0.6 percent, which was in line with expectations.
Dealers said the market is now focused on the release next Friday of Canadian and U.S. employment data. Otherwise, Canada has a very sparse calender of data in the coming week.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.13 to C$104.25 to yield 6.405 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The negative spread between the Canadian and U.S. benchmark bonds widened to 15 basis points from 14 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.91 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.22 percent.
